content.text:
You are a veteran Capcom NES pixel artist and art director for Mega Man 2-3. You are shown ONE small enemy sprite,
at 1x (true size, left) and enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling (right), on a neutral grey-blue background
that is not part of the sprite.

The sprite is supposed to be this enemy:
"A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes."
Intended size: about 16x16 to 20x20 px. Game: Mega Man 2-3 (NES).

Judge whether it is a convincing authentic NES Mega Man enemy that matches the description. Be calibrated:
authentic Capcom enemy sprites score about 90-95; competent fan art about 60-70; amateur or AI-looking pixel art
about 30-45. Do not reward or punish a sprite for being recognisable; judge what you see.

Criteria, 0-10 each:
- authenticity: could ship unchanged in MM2/MM3 (Capcom conventions, not "modern pixel art")
- description_fidelity: matches the description (body, features, role)
- readability_1x: the silhouette and features read instantly at true size
- pixel_craft: 1-px black outlines used the Capcom way, clean clusters, no jaggies, orphans, dithering or noise
- palette_discipline: NES colours, flat shading with at most one highlight, about 3 colours + transparent per 8x8 tile
- appeal: charm and character in the Capcom manner

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"subscores": {"authenticity": n, "description_fidelity": n, "readability_1x": n, "pixel_craft": n,
  "palette_discipline": n, "appeal": n},
 "score": 0-100 overall,
 "verdict": "convincing" or "not_convincing",
 "issues": ["specific, located problems"],
 "fixes": ["specific pixel-level fixes"]}

message.content: {"subscores":{"authenticity":5,"description_fidelity":8,"readability_1x":6,"pixel_craft":5,"palette_discipline":6,"appeal":6},"score":60,"verdict":"not_convincing","issues":["The thick black horizontal band across the lower body visually separates the face from the tentacles instead of describing a clean squid form.","The large white block on the right reads as a rectangular side appendage rather than part of a rounded mantle.","At 1x, the asymmetrical red-and-black eye clusters become noisy and do not read as a clean matched pair.","The lower cyan tentacles merge into a dense diagonal staircase, weakening the gather-and-thrust silhouette.","Several outline transitions around the eye boxes and lower-right body are heavier and more angular than typical MM2/MM3 Capcom clusters.","The sprite uses black, white, bright cyan, dark cyan, and red in close proximity, making the implied NES sprite-palette construction less disciplined."],"fixes":["Reduce the central horizontal black band to a one-pixel contour and reconnect the mantle to the tentacle base.","Round off the right white mass by removing its outer corner pixels and cap it with a cyan or black mantle contour.","Simplify both eyes into matching white sockets with one red flash pixel or compact red pupils; remove excess internal black pixels.","Separate the tentacles into two or three distinct one- to two-pixel-wide lobes with clear negative-space gaps.","Replace the long diagonal cyan staircase in the lower center with larger, cleaner clusters and a more symmetrical thrust pose.","Keep each component sprite to black plus two body colors or black, white, and red, reserving dark cyan for a separate, clearly tiled shadow component."]}
